title: Five statements and a promise
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What are the five things your audience should remember?
Jose asked a student to present a deck as if to a client, and said he would give a cue to stop and analyze it, so the group could collaborate on how the presentation is built.
A student who presented said that it showed why being prepared is key, and that the worst thing is just reading off the slides.
Jose said that a student's sentence was very concise and specific, and to write it down. He said the aim is to have no more than a few points.

He said: take five statements from the presentation, remembering simple, repeatable, relevant. He said that you could call the opening a promise: our promise in this presentation is to show you how we see the relationship.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write your promise in one line.
Present to a friend and ask for a stop cue.
Write what you will not read off the slide.

check.q: What did Jose say to do with a presentation?
What did a student say is the worst thing?
What did Jose say you could call the opening?

recap: Five statements, simple, relevant and repeatable. Open with a promise.
